transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora. I've just done your post-cataract surgery follow-up check with you. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or how you're getting on with your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. So you should be fine to get back to that fairly soon. Just avoid anything too strenuous or heavy lifting for about a month.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes again?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

Just make sure you store it as directed on the bottle - some need to be kept in the fridge and others at room temperature.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I do. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Some sensitivity to light is quite normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses, and we'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if the light sensitivity is severe or you're also experiencing a red and painful eye, that's not normal and we may need to check that further. 

Is yours mild, or are you having significant pain and redness as well?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Mine is just mild sensitivity. I haven't noticed any pain or redness.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's good to hear. In that case, just wear your sunglasses when you're out and about, and your eyes should adjust over time.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, one more. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It depends on how long it's been since your surgery. It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after the operation, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How long ago was your surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It was about two weeks ago.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
At two weeks, some mild blurriness can still be normal as your eyes continue to settle. However, if your vision is getting significantly worse or remains quite blurry, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

Is the blurriness staying about the same, improving, or getting worse?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It's been gradually improving, so I think it's just part of the healing process. Thank you for all the information. I don't have any more questions right now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's great to hear that your vision is improving - that's a positive sign!

Just to confirm, have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thank you for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and don't hesitate to get in touch if you have any concerns during your recovery.

verdict.label: pass
